Mecca is the holiest city in Islam, located in western Saudi Arabia, and the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. Every year, millions of Muslim pilgrims from around the world converge on Mecca to perform the hajj, one of the Five Pillars of Islam. The city is home to the Kaaba, a cubic shrine that Muslims believe was originally built by Abraham and is the spiritual center of Islamic worship.

Muhammad was born in Mecca around five hundred seventy CE. He preached there initially but was forced to flee to Medina in six hundred twenty-two CE in the Hijra, or migration, an event that marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. The Kaaba is a cube-shaped structure covered in black cloth standing at the center of the al-Masjid al-Haram, the Sacred Mosque. Muslims believe it to be the house of God on Earth, originally built by Abraham and his son Ishmael.

The Hajj, performed in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah, is a pilgrimage that every adult Muslim able to do so is required to undertake at least once in their lifetime. It is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. The circumambulation of the Kaaba, called tawaf, and other rituals of the hajj commemorate events in the life of Abraham and Ishmael and symbolize the unity and equality of all Muslims before God. Mecca is considered haram, or sacred, and non-Muslims are forbidden to enter the city. Muslims consider it the spiritual heart of the Islamic world.
